title: Tuilaepa Pushes Three Controversial Constitutional Bills
reason: Independent sources confirm all material details. Samoa's Parliament passed three bills — the Constitution Amendment Bill 2020, Land and Titles Bill 2020, and Judicature Bill 2020 — on 15 December 2020 (vote 41-4), under PM Tuilaepa Sailele Malielegaoi's HRPP government. The bills restructured the judiciary, creating a parallel Land and Titles High Court/Court of Appeal for customary land and titles (matai) matters and removing appeals to the ordinary Supreme Court/Court of Appeal. Critics — Samoa's judiciary, the Samoa Law Society, the government's own Ombudsman, the UN Special Rapporteur on judicial independence, and Amnesty International — warned the reforms eroded judicial independence and violated ICCPR Article 14.
